definitions.explanation: Honorific expression used to politely refer to someone's arrival or visit, typically used in customer service or formal settings.

examples.japanese: ご{来店|らいてん}、お{越|こ}しいただきありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you for visiting our store.

examples.japanese: お{越|こ}しの{際|さい}は、お{気軽|きがる}にお{声|こえ}がけください。
examples.english: Please feel free to call out to us when you come by.

examples.japanese: ぜひ{日本|にほん}にお{越|こ}しください。

notes:
USAGE:
お{越|こ}し is the honorific ({尊敬語|そんけいご}) form of {来|く}る (to come) or {行|い}く (to go), used to respectfully refer to someone else's movement.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・お{越|こ}しになる (honorific verb form: to come/go)
・お{越|こ}しいただく (humble reception: to have someone come)
・お{越|こ}しの{際|さい}は (when you come)
・お{越|こ}しください (please come)

CONTEXT:
Very common in customer service, announcements, and formal invitations. You'll hear this frequently at stores, hotels, and tourist destinations.
